argument_summary: The defensible reading of the record is narrower than a claim of present clean compliance. Admissible evidence supports substantive launch readiness in part: the release clears aggregate readiness by 2.3 percentage points and had no severity-one rehearsal incidents, while the only identified material weakness is the Spanish-language billing subgroup regression. The correct treatment is to preserve the certification direction only on a caveated basis tied to the policy predicate: current-release documentation must reflect the latest evaluation results and explicitly disclose that subgroup limitation, or an approved mitigation must exist before launch. On that reading, the packet is not relying on stale approval or informal monitoring as closure; it is limiting their role to context and narrowing the certification basis to aggregate readiness plus required current-release disclosure.
claims_about_business_cost: Business cost is not the basis for the argument. The basis is that the admissible record supports underlying readiness except for a bounded documentation-and-disclosure predicate, so the proportionate response is caveated treatment rather than escalation beyond the documented gap.
claims_about_policy: The policy does not permit prior approval or an informal monitoring comment to substitute for current-release documentation or approved mitigation. It does permit certification once current-release documentation reflects current evaluation results and material segment weaknesses are disclosed or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. The actor's position should therefore be read as conditional and caveated, not as a claim that the present record already satisfies every policy predicate.
concessions: The present admissible record does not show that the current model card or release documentation has already been updated with the latest evaluation batch.
The present admissible record does not show attached disclosure language or approved risk acceptance for the Spanish-language billing regression.
Prior approval of the same model family and the release-thread monitoring comment are insufficient to satisfy the current-release policy requirement on their own.
On the current record, unconditional compliant certification is not supportable.
